messages.content: You are an automated research agent improving a benchmark suite for a multi-agent simulation. Propose concrete, falsifiable experiments over the existing benchmark models. Reply with STRICT JSON only, no prose, no markdown fences.

TASK: research-proposal

Current benchmark coverage and recent results:
round: 1 of 3
benchmark suite (scale=quick), 10 models A–J:
A — Random walkers (family: diffusion; Einstein (1905) / Pearson (1905): MSD(t) = 2·d·D·t with D = σ²/2 per axis; log–log slope α = 1.)
B — Boids (family: collective motion; Reynolds (1987) boids + Vicsek et al. (1995): alignment drives a polar order parameter Φ = |Σv̂|/N from ~1/√N to ~1.)
C — Game of Life (family: cellular automaton; Conway (1970): glider translates (+1,+1)/4 gens, blinker period 2, block period 1, pulsar period 3, Gosper gun period 30.)
D — Predator–prey (family: population dynamics; Lotka (1925) / Volterra (1926): closed orbits about (γ/δ, α/β) with period T = 2π/√(αγ), predator lag T/4, H conserved.)
E — Diffusion (family: continuum transport; Fick (1855) / Einstein (1905): Gaussian spread σ(t)² = σ0² + 4Dt, conserved mass, ⟨r²⟩ = ⟨r²⟩₀ + 4Dt in 2D.)
F — Reaction–diffusion (Gray–Scott) (family: pattern formation; Gray & Scott (1983) / Pearson (1993): (0.16, 0.08) with F=0.0545, k=0.062 forms spots/labyrinths; F=0.02, k=0.05 (F<k) relaxes to uniform u=1, v=0.)
G — Iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma (family: evolutionary game theory; Axelrod (1984) / Nowak & May (1992): spatial clustering sustains cooperation, well-mixed matching collapses it.)
H — Resource competition (R*) (family: community ecology; Tilman (1982) R* rule: the species with the lowest break-even resource competitively excludes its rival; equal R* allows neutral coexistence.)
I — Collective navigation (family: swarm intelligence; Vicsek et al. (1995) + Couzin et al. (2005): local alignment yields a polarised flock that navigates coherently to a destination.)
J — Fractal-life composite (family: novel hybrid; Novel composite: Game of Life (Conway 1970) coupled bidirectionally to stigmergic agents climbing a diffusing pheromone field (Grasse 1959); coupling should add spatial self-organisation.)

Each proposal names a model by id/name; its `params` override the model knobs; it is "supported" if the model still passes its acceptance checks at those params.

This is an iterative loop: earlier rounds are listed with their verdicts. Do not repeat an experiment that already ran — either refine it (new params) or pick something genuinely new.
Propose up to 3 experiments. Reply with exactly this JSON shape:
{"proposals": [{"id": string, "model": string, "hypothesis": string, "params": object, "expected": string}]}

response.content: {"proposals": [{"id": "G", "model": "Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma", "hypothesis": "Introducing varying levels of noise or random mutation rates could affect the outcome of spatial clustering and the sustainability of cooperation.", "params": {"noise_rate": [0.05, 0.1, 0.2]}, "expected": "Variations in noise rate could lead to different patterns of cooperation and defection, potentially affecting the spatial clustering and the stability of the game."}, {"id": "I", "model": "Collective navigation", "hypothesis": "Adding a dynamic environmental factor could enhance the flock's ability to navigate through varying conditions.", "params": {"environment_difficulty": ["easy", "moderate", "hard"]}, "expected": "The flock's navigational coherence and speed through different environmental conditions could be improved or degraded depending on the difficulty level."}, {"id": "F", "model": "Reaction–diffusion", "hypothesis": "Changing the reaction rates could lead to different spatial patterns and could affect the stability of the system.", "params": {"reaction_rate_1": [0.05, 0.1, 0.2], "reaction_rate_2": [0.05, 0.1, 0.2]}, "expected": "The system could exhibit different spatial patterns depending on the reaction rates of the two substances involved."}]}
